newsitem.title: USA: Amy Fisher loses chance for parole in NY.
newsitem.headline: Amy Fisher loses chance for parole in NY.

text.p: Amy Fisher, the teenager who shot her lover's wife in a case that grabbed national headlines, has lost her chance for parole, state prison officials said Thursday.

Fisher, now 22, is serving five to 15 years at the Albion State Prison in western New York for first-degree assault in the 1992 shooting of Mary Jo Buttafuoco, 42. She will be held for an additional 24 months and can appear before the state parole board again in June 1999.

Fisher was interviewed Tuesday and the board made the decision public Thursday. A native of Massapequa, Long Island, she was dubbed the "Long Island Lolita" for her involvement with Joey Buttafuoco, a married man with two children.
She shot Mary Jo Buttafuoco in the head with a .25 calibre handgun after an argument at the Buttafuoco home.

The board told Fisher she was denied parole because "there is a reasonable probability that you would not live and remain at liberty without violating the law and your release at this time is incompatible with the welfare and safety of the community."
Parole officials also said she had had a chance to stop the crime and failed to do so. "You planned it and you carried it out," the parole report said.

It also criticised her for failing to get aid for her victim, saying she went home instead to clean the blood off herself. "Your pattern of intention and the severity of your criminal act coupled with your lack of insight into your criminality do make your discretionary release not appropriate at this time," the parole report concluded.

Mary Jo Buttafuoco gave testimony to parole officials in May asking them to keep Fisher in prison, saying she had suffered agony and humiliation since she was shot by Fisher. She still has the bullet in her head and now lives in California, raising her two children alone.
Fisher's affair with Joey Buttafuoco and the shooting became a national story and the subject of several television movies.
